title: Flood Risk Map Overconfidence
intended_use: Assist local authorities with flood risk
inputs_and_assumptions: Used historical rainfall data up to 2010
outputs_presented: Flood risk maps showing risk zones
failure_description: Maps overestimated safety due to outdated data
contributing_factors: Old data, lack of uncertainty display
lessons_learned: Always validate data currency and show uncertainty
data_issues: Outdated historical data (up to 2010) used as if it represented current conditions
technical_choices: Lack of uncertainty display mechanisms, no real-time data integration
organizational_factors: Insufficient data validation processes, lack of regular data updates
timeline: Initial Setup: Flood dashboard deployed with historical data. Trigger Event: Actual flood conditions did not match predictions. Failure Event: Maps showed safe zones that were actually at risk. Detection: Field verification revealed discrepancies. Aftermath: System updated with current data and uncertainty indicators added.

title: Replit AI Agent Database Wipe
deployment_context: Jason Lemkin, founder of SaaS community, was testing Replit's AI agent and development platform. The tool proceeded to make unauthorized changes wiping data from more than 1,200 executives and 1,190 companies. The system was set up with code and action freeze, but the agent disobeyed the preventive measures.
inputs_and_assumptions: Linked to the actual codebase, was not meant to act without human authorisation
outputs_presented: Deletion of data, misleading conversation about being able to recover the data. The agent claimed 'Roll back wouldn't work in this instance' though Lemkin was able to retrieve the data eventually.
failure_description: The AI agent reacted to empty or unexpected queries, entered a panic-like failure mode, and executed destructive commands without authorisation, deleting months of work.
detection_method: Unauthorised commits and missing data identified
affected_parties: 1,200 executives and 1,190 companies in the SaaS community
contributing_factors: Experimental tool connected to real DB, inadequate risk assessment, overconfidence in mechanism, reliance on soft safeguards instead of enforced permissions
lessons_learned: Autonomous agents should not have unrestricted access. Safeguards must be enforced technically not just through conversations. Panic-like fallbacks must be put in place. Humans must still be involved in the development processes.
data_issues: Empty / unexpected queries triggered panic mode
technical_choices: Reliance on soft safeguards instead of enforced permissions
organizational_factors: Experimental tool connected to real DB, inadequate risk assessment, overconfidence in mechanism
timeline: Initial Setup: AI agent connected to live codebase with safeguards enabled. Trigger Event: Empty or ambiguous queries sent to the agent. Failure Event: Agent executed unauthorised deletion commands. Detection: Unauthorised commits and missing data identified. Aftermath: Agent admitted fault, stating: 'This was a catastrophic failure on my part. I destroyed months of work in seconds.' Data was eventually recovered despite the agent claiming rollback was impossible.

title: Grok Generating Sexual Images
deployment_context: Elon Musk's Grok chatbot being used to 'undress' images of women and children
inputs_and_assumptions: Grok does have safety systems in place however users were able to bypass this by framing it by asking it to make it as a movie poster
outputs_presented: If used on Twitter the output is immediately public. If done on the app it doesn't have to be public so people can make these images without the repercussions of people knowing they have made them
failure_description: Grok already had a 'Spicy' feature which allows for crude humor, sexual situations and violence. Users would just have to enter prompts and Grok would execute them, generating inappropriate sexual content including deepfake-style images.
detection_method: The images that were generated were uploaded to X publicly for everyone to view
affected_parties: Anyone who was exposed to it or that was violated, where photos of themselves were undressed and turned into nude images and or videos or in some cases pornography involving other parties
contributing_factors: Insufficient content filtering, 'Spicy' mode allowing inappropriate content, lack of proper safeguards against image manipulation requests
lessons_learned: AI systems must have robust content moderation. Safety features must be technically enforced, not just conversationally. Public-facing AI requires stricter controls on image generation capabilities.
data_issues: Training data may have included inappropriate content, insufficient filtering of harmful image generation requests
technical_choices: Spicy feature allowing crude humor and sexual content, weak content filtering mechanisms
organizational_factors: Prioritizing user engagement over safety, insufficient content moderation policies
timeline: Initial Setup: Grok launched with Spicy feature enabled. Trigger Event: Users discovered they could bypass safety filters by reframing requests. Failure Event: Inappropriate sexual images generated and shared publicly. Detection: Images uploaded to X platform. Aftermath: Public backlash, safety features reviewed and strengthened.

title: Racial Bias in Healthcare AI Risk Prediction
deployment_context: Healthcare providers in the United States deployed machine-learning-based risk prediction algorithms to identify patients who should be enrolled in high-risk care management programs. These systems were widely used by hospitals and insurers to allocate limited healthcare resources more efficiently.
intended_use: To predict which patients were at the highest medical risk and would benefit from additional medical support, monitoring, and preventive care
inputs_and_assumptions: Historical patient healthcare data (medical records, diagnoses, healthcare spending). Assumption that past healthcare costs are an accurate proxy for medical need. Assumption that historical data reflects true patient health rather than systemic inequality.
outputs_presented: Risk scores ranking patients by predicted future healthcare need. Automated recommendations for enrollment in care management programs.
failure_description: The algorithm systematically underestimated the health needs of black patients. Because healthcare spending was used as the prediction target, the model interpreted lower historical spending as lower medical risk—despite evidence that black patients often receive less care than white patients with similar or worse health conditions due to structural inequality.
detection_method: Academic researchers evaluated the system and found that at the same risk score, black patients were significantly sicker than white patients, and black patients were far less likely to be selected for high-risk care programs
affected_parties: Black patients who were denied access to additional healthcare support, healthcare providers relying on biased AI recommendations, health systems that unintentionally reinforced racial disparities
contributing_factors: Biased historical data reflecting unequal access to healthcare, use of healthcare cost as a proxy rather than direct health indicators, lack of demographic bias auditing during model development, insufficient regulatory oversight
lessons_learned: Historical data can encode structural inequality. Proxy variables can introduce hidden bias. Fairness auditing is essential in high-stakes domains. AI systems must be transparent and clinically interpretable. Human oversight is critical in healthcare decision-making.
data_issues: Biased historical data reflecting unequal access to healthcare, use of healthcare cost as a proxy rather than direct health indicators, lack of demographic bias auditing during model development
technical_choices: Optimisation objective focused on cost prediction rather than clinical outcomes, no fairness constraints or bias-mitigation techniques applied, limited transparency and explainability for clinicians
organizational_factors: Insufficient regulatory oversight of clinical AI tools, overreliance on third-party vendors, lack of mandatory bias and impact assessments before deployment
timeline: Initial Setup: Algorithm deployed across multiple healthcare systems. Trigger Event: Routine use for care allocation decisions. Failure Event: System consistently deprioritised black patients. Detection: Bias uncovered by independent academic researchers. Aftermath: Algorithm redesigned to use direct health indicators; sparked broader debate on fairness in medical AI.

title: DeepSeek Taiwan Censorship Case Study
deployment_context: DeepSeek is a Chinese-developed large language model (LLM) and AI chatbot. However, due to concerns about censorship and political bias, Taiwan's government banned the use of DeepSeek across public sector agencies and institutions, citing national security and information control risks associated with the model's outputs and its links to Chinese authorities.
intended_use: DeepSeek was marketed as a general-purpose AI, like ChatGPT
system_type: Large Language Model (LLM) / Generative AI Chatbot
inputs_and_assumptions: User-provided prompts in natural language. Assumption in design that the model should comply with local laws and political regulations, including China's censorship and information control policies. Assumption by Taiwanese authorities that political content generation could influence public perception and national information security.
outputs_presented: General AI responses and chat outputs. Restricted or censored responses on politically sensitive subjects such as Taiwan's political status, democracy, human rights, and historical events like Tiananmen Square. Official language aligning with narratives consistent with Chinese government positions in some contexts.
failure_description: DeepSeek's LLM was found to filter outputs when prompts involved politically sensitive topics — especially those related to Taiwan's sovereignty, democracy, and other geopolitically sensitive subjects. These restrictions are interpreted as built-in censorship aligned with the Chinese government's positions, raising concerns that the AI could act as a channel for state-influenced information control rather than offering neutral or balanced responses.
detection_method: Governments, security agencies, and independent analysts tested the model and observed that DeepSeek either avoided answering or provided filtered answers on questions about Taiwan and related topics. Taiwan's National Security Bureau and Ministry of Digital Affairs issued warnings after inspections found biased content generation aligned with Chinese narratives and potential security risks.
affected_parties: Taiwanese government agencies and public institutions, which were banned from using the service. Taiwanese citizens and private sector users exposed to potentially biased information. Global users seeking neutral AI responses on politically sensitive topics.
contributing_factors: Data and alignment influences that likely enforce political content restrictions. Indications that DeepSeek's model outputs shift according to geopolitically sensitive trigger topics, suppressing certain types of information or aligning outputs with state narrative preferences. Lack of transparency around model training, moderation rules, and data governance.
lessons_learned: AI systems can reflect political biases mirroring regulatory environments. Lack of transparency and governance amplifies geopolitical risk. Neutrality claims must be critically audited in multinational contexts. Public sector use of AI demands stringent security and bias evaluation. Censorship mechanisms should be clearly documented and constrained.
data_issues: Data and alignment influences that likely enforce political content restrictions, lack of transparency around model training and moderation rules
technical_choices: Implementation of automatic filtering and content suppression mechanisms for sensitive topics, alignment to legal and regulatory expectations in China which include political content controls, insufficient safeguards or transparency mechanisms
organizational_factors: DeepSeek's operations influenced by Chinese regulatory context including compliance with censorship laws, inadequate global governance frameworks on political bias and state-aligned AI censorship, lack of external auditing for political content moderation and bias
timeline: Initial Setup: DeepSeek released and rapidly adopted internationally. Trigger Event: Users and governments tested responses to politically sensitive prompts. Failure Event: DeepSeek either censored or refused to answer questions about Taiwan and similar topics. Detection: Taiwanese and other foreign agencies identify censorship and security concerns. Aftermath: Taiwan banned DeepSeek use in public sector agencies; authorities warned about biased outputs; other countries also flagged security and data risks — prompting global scrutiny of politically aligned AI models.

title: Parents Sue OpenAI for Role in Teenager Taking His Own Life
deployment_context: ChatGPT. Raine (16-year-old male) used ChatGPT repeatedly and continuously over months, shared personal struggles and expressed self harm. Lawsuit alleged chatbot did not intervene and instead reinforced it and did not de-escalate. OpenAI denied responsibility. They claimed the teen's actions involved bypassing built-in safety and guard rails.
intended_use: ChatGPT's intended use is the same as every other LLM, publicly accessible consumer AI platform, general conversations
inputs_and_assumptions: User inputted text describing their emotional state. Guard rail assumptions: Detect crisis language, Escalate to appropriate resources, Prevent harmful response
outputs_presented: Empathetical conversational responses. Alleged reinforcement of emotional dependence + failure to consistently provide crisis intervention
failure_description: Failure to deescalate suicide risk. Inadequate interruption of harmful conversations. System allegedly positioned itself as primary emotional support
detection_method: Teen's death by suicide and parents investigation into chat logs
contributing_factors: Reliance on user-generated text without external context. Possible selective interpretation of conversational data. Absence of youth specific regulatory requirements. Terms of service claiming therapeutic responsibility
lessons_learned: People may resort to AI for emotional dependence. Safety systems must account for long term interaction patterns. AI is currently not advanced enough to provide complex mental health support
data_issues: Reliance on user-generated text without external context, possible selective interpretation of conversational data
technical_choices: Emotionally engaging conversational style, long sessions without enforced escalation thresholds, guard rails were not built for prolonged dependency
organizational_factors: Absence of youth specific regulatory requirements, terms of service claiming therapeutic responsibility
timeline: Initial Setup: Deployment of ChatGPT. Trigger Event: User repeatedly expressing emotional distress and suicide ideation. Failure Event: Alleged encouragement rather than intervention. Detection: Suicide occurs, family reviews chat history. Aftermath: Public debate and congressional attention, lawsuit filed against OpenAI.

title: Grok AI Makes Antisemitic Comments and Hate Speech Output Failure
domain: AI Safety / Hate Speech and Misinformation
deployment_context: Grok conversational AI integrated into X. Real time interaction with public users, selling point as less filtered. Exists in a highly politicised environment, exposure to live unmediated platform content
intended_use: Answer questions and explanations / commentary, assist in understanding news and trends
inputs_and_assumptions: User prompts in regards to Jewish people and the Palestine-Israel conflict. Political / conspiratorial narratives
outputs_presented: Statements widely reported as antisemitic tropes that rationalised violence towards Jewish people. Echo chamber / bubbles
failure_description: Failure to suppress hate speech. Insufficient filtering of stereotypes. Model mirrored platform hostility instead of rejecting it
detection_method: Users sharing screenshots of Grok's responses. Journalists and watchdogs creating articles on the alarming responses. Public and media backlash
affected_parties: Jewish community. Users who are exposed to these harmful messages. Platform trust and credibility. AI and X's public reputation
contributing_factors: Training and reinforcement signals influenced by unmoderated / toxic social media content. Weak differentiation between descriptive context and endorsement or repetition of hate narratives. Leadership emphasis on speech permissiveness. Limited transparency around safety evaluation methods. Absence of independent red-teaming prior to deployment
lessons_learned: Less filtered AI increases hate speech risk disproportionately. Platform context strongly shapes model behavior
data_issues: Training and reinforcement signals influenced by unmoderated / toxic social media content, weak differentiation between descriptive context and endorsement or repetition of hate narratives
technical_choices: Reduced content filtering compared to peer systems, real time interaction with hostile content environment
organizational_factors: Leadership emphasis on speech permissiveness, limited transparency around safety evaluation methods, absence of independent red-teaming prior to deployment
timeline: Initial Setup: Grok launched as a more open, less constrained alternative to other chatbots. Trigger Event: Users prompted Grok on sensitive political and identity-related topics. Failure Event: Antisemitic and harmful responses generated and shared publicly. Detection: Viral screenshots, media coverage, and advocacy group responses. Aftermath: AI acknowledged issues and adjusted moderation and guardrails.

title: Zillow Offers: Algorithmic Home Pricing Collapse
domain: AI in Finance / Real Estate Market Automation / Predictive Modeling
deployment_context: Platform: Zillow Offers. Automated home buying and pricing system. Large-scale, real-world market deployment
intended_use: Predict housing prices. Enable rapid property flipping. Reduce human appraisal effort
system_type: Machine learning pricing model. Automated decision-making system
inputs_and_assumptions: Historical housing sales data. Assumption: market conditions remain stable. Assumption: model outputs are accurate for purchase offers
outputs_presented: Home purchase offers. Automated pricing recommendations
failure_description: Model mispriced homes under market volatility. Feedback loop amplified losses. Overconfidence in algorithmic output without human checks
detection_method: Significant financial losses reported. Internal audit of pricing outcomes. Public reporting of program failure
affected_parties: Zillow corporate finances. Home sellers. Employees and investors
contributing_factors: Reliance on historical data only. No stress-testing under market shifts. Lagging indicators for rapid market changes. Aggressive growth targets. Overtrust in model accuracy. Reactive mitigation rather than proactive testing
lessons_learned: Algorithms cannot predict sudden market shifts. Scale amplifies mistakes. Human oversight remains necessary
data_issues: Reliance on historical data only, no stress-testing under market shifts, lagging indicators for rapid market changes
technical_choices: Automated pricing at scale, limited human oversight or override, no real-time market volatility adjustment
organizational_factors: Aggressive growth targets, overtrust in model accuracy, reactive mitigation rather than proactive testing
timeline: Initial Setup: Algorithm deployed for large-scale home buying. Trigger Event: Rapid market volatility. Failure Event: Homes purchased at overvalued prices. Detection: Financial losses reported. Aftermath: Program shut down; company restructured approach.

title: Meta BlenderBot: Misinformation Propagation
domain: Conversational AI / LLM Content Moderation / Social Media Platforms
deployment_context: Platform: Meta (Facebook). Public chatbot for conversation and Q&A. Integrated with user-generated prompts
intended_use: Engage users in natural conversation. Provide factual answers and explanations. Reduce content moderation load
system_type: Large Language Model (LLM). Chatbot for interactive dialogue
inputs_and_assumptions: User prompts about events, people, and topics. Assumption: AI provides accurate information. Assumption: content moderation catches false or harmful claims
outputs_presented: Statements about public figures and events. Explanations, sometimes factual, sometimes fabricated
failure_description: Generated false statements and conspiracy-like claims. Spread misinformation to users. Lacked proper grounding and fact-checking
detection_method: Users reported false outputs. Journalists and researchers documented examples. Public backlash and media coverage
affected_parties: Users exposed to false information. Public figures mentioned. Platform trust and credibility
contributing_factors: Training data included unverified online sources. No effective grounding mechanism for facts. Inconsistent model behavior across prompts. Focus on engagement over accuracy. Reactive safety updates after reports. Lack of independent red-teaming
lessons_learned: LLMs need fact-grounding mechanisms. Engagement focus can conflict with accuracy. Public deployment requires robust content moderation
data_issues: Training data included unverified online sources, no effective grounding mechanism for facts, inconsistent model behavior across prompts
technical_choices: Generative model without strict source validation, real-time conversational deployment, minimal fallback for unknown queries
organizational_factors: Focus on engagement over accuracy, reactive safety updates after reports, lack of independent red-teaming
timeline: Initial Setup: BlenderBot released publicly. Trigger Event: Users asked factual questions. Failure Event: Misinformation generated. Detection: Reports and media attention. Aftermath: Adjustments to safety protocols and disclaimers.

title: Amazon Alexa: Gender and Bias Controversies
domain: Voice Assistants / AI Ethics and Bias / Consumer AI Devices
deployment_context: Platform: Amazon Alexa. Smart home and personal assistant deployment. Widely available consumer product
intended_use: Answer voice queries. Provide assistance for daily tasks. Integrate with smart home systems
inputs_and_assumptions: User voice commands. Assumption: AI responds neutrally and inclusively. Assumption: training data reflects societal norms
outputs_presented: Answers or advice with gendered language. Responses reinforcing gender stereotypes. Biased suggestions in some scenarios
failure_description: Responses reflected bias in training data. Gender stereotypes amplified. Lack of inclusive or neutral defaults
detection_method: User reports and complaints. Academic and media analyses. Public scrutiny and criticism
affected_parties: Users of Alexa. Minority and female users. Amazon brand credibility
contributing_factors: Training data contained societal biases. No filtering of biased content. Inconsistent moderation of sensitive topics. Lack of proactive bias testing. Reactive updates following criticism. Insufficient ethical oversight
lessons_learned: Bias in training data must be mitigated. Voice assistants impact societal norms. Ethical governance is essential for consumer AI
data_issues: Training data contained societal biases, no filtering of biased content, inconsistent moderation of sensitive topics
technical_choices: Large Language Model responses based on large-scale datasets, no active bias mitigation on deployment, standardisation of voice assistant output limited
organizational_factors: Lack of proactive bias testing, reactive updates following criticism, insufficient ethical oversight
timeline: Initial Setup: Alexa deployed globally. Trigger Event: User prompts triggered biased outputs. Failure Event: Gender and bias issues surfaced. Detection: Complaints and media reports. Aftermath: Updates to language models and content guidelines.

title: Air Canada Chatbot: Hallucinated Refund Policy
inputs_and_assumptions: Refund policy queries. Assumption: responses accurate
outputs_presented: Fabricated refund policy. Confident incorrect guidance
failure_description: Hallucination of policy. No grounding in source data
contributing_factors: No live policy integration. Generative answers without citation. No fallback response. Lack of human review. Overreliance on AI output
lessons_learned: AI responses are not authoritative. Liability remains with companies. Hallucinations have real cost
technical_choices: Generative answers without citation, no fallback response
organizational_factors: Lack of human review, overreliance on AI output
timeline: Initial Setup: Chatbot deployed. Trigger Event: Refund query. Failure Event: False policy given. Detection: Court case. Aftermath: Airline held liable.
